Sample Size or Power for a Treatment Effect in a Two-Level Mixed-Effects Model

Source: R/ss_power_mixed_effects.R
ss_power_mixed_effects.Rd

Determine the necessary number of clusters (i.e., Level 2 units) per arm to achieve a desired level of statistical power for a treatment-versus-control comparison in a two-level mixed-effects model with a random intercept (e.g., individuals nested within clusters in a cluster-randomized trial, or repeated measurements nested within subjects in a person-randomized longitudinal study). Alternatively, given a number of clusters per arm, return the realized statistical power.

Usage

ss_power_mixed_effects(
  true_smd,
  cluster_size,
  true_icc,
  specified_n_clusters_per_arm = NULL,
  desired_power = 0.85,
  alpha_level = 0.05,
  directional = FALSE
)

Arguments

true_smd

Population standardized treatment effect the test is powered for (\(d\) in the formulas below), defined as the population mean difference divided by the population standard deviation of the outcome among individual observations (i.e., Level 1 units)

cluster_size

Number of observations (i.e., Level 1 units) in each cluster (i.e., Level 2 unit); for example, individuals per cluster or measurements per subject, \(n\) in the formulas below; a single whole number of at least 2, assumed equal across clusters. It has no default

true_icc

Population intraclass correlation (the proportion of total outcome variance attributable to differences between clusters (i.e., Level 2 units)), \(\rho\) in the formulas below; a planning value that must be in [0, 1)

specified_n_clusters_per_arm

Number of clusters (i.e., Level 2 units) in each arm, \(J\) in the formulas below (i.e., specified_n_clusters_per_arm treatment clusters and as many control clusters, so the total number of clusters is twice this value); if specified, returns the realized power

desired_power

Desired statistical power (default 0.85)

alpha_level

Type I error rate (default 0.05)

directional

Logical: TRUE for a one-sided test (in the same sign as true_smd), FALSE (default) for a two-sided test

Value

A data.frame with rows for necessary_n_clusters_per_arm (or specified_n_clusters_per_arm when specified_n_clusters_per_arm is given), total_N (the total number of observations (i.e., Level 1 units), \(2 J n\)), noncentral_t_parm (the noncentrality parameter \(\lambda\) of the t distribution), and actual_power. The result carries the dmar_ss_power class, so tidy and glance summarize it in broom convention (the reported size is the number of clusters per arm).

Details

This function computes power for the fixed treatment effect at the higher level of a two-level mixed-effects model with random intercept, $$y_{ij} = \beta_0 + \beta_1 T_j + u_j + \epsilon_{ij},$$ where \(u_j \sim N(0, \sigma_u^2)\) is the cluster (i.e., Level 2) random intercept and \(\epsilon_{ij} \sim N(0, \sigma_e^2)\) is the within-cluster (i.e., Level 1) residual. The treatment indicator \(T_j\) varies between clusters (i.e., entire clusters or entire subjects are assigned to treatment or control). The intra-class correlation is \(\rho = \sigma_u^2 / (\sigma_u^2 + \sigma_e^2)\) and the total outcome variance is \(\sigma_y^2 = \sigma_u^2 + \sigma_e^2\).

With \(n\) observations in each cluster (cluster_size) and \(J\) clusters in each arm (specified_n_clusters_per_arm), the standard error of the estimated treatment effect is \(SE(\hat\beta_1) = \sigma_y \sqrt{2 (1 + (n - 1)\rho) / (J n)}\), giving a noncentrality parameter of $$\lambda = d \sqrt{J n / (2 (1 + (n - 1)\rho))}$$ under a two-sample t-test with \(2J - 2\) degrees of freedom.

The factor \(1 + (n - 1)\rho\) is the design effect: as the within-cluster correlation grows, the effective information per cluster shrinks, so more clusters are needed for a given level of power.

References

Maxwell, S. E., Delaney, H. D., & Kelley, K. (2027). Designing experiments and analyzing data: A model comparison perspective (4th ed.). Routledge.

Raudenbush, S. W. (1997). Statistical analysis and optimal design for cluster randomized trials. Psychological Methods, 2, 173–185. doi:10.1037/1082-989X.2.2.173

Ken Kelley kkelley@nd.edu

Examples

# 30 individuals per cluster, ICC = 0.05, standardized effect 0.30, power = .80
ss_power_mixed_effects(true_smd = 0.30, cluster_size = 30, true_icc = 0.05, desired_power = 0.80)
#>  term                         value
#>  necessary_n_clusters_per_arm 16   
#>  total_N                      960  
#>  noncentral_t_parm            2.969
#>  actual_power                 0.819

# Same effect but with much higher ICC (e.g., schools or therapists)
ss_power_mixed_effects(true_smd = 0.30, cluster_size = 30, true_icc = 0.20, desired_power = 0.80)
#>  term                         value
#>  necessary_n_clusters_per_arm 41   
#>  total_N                      2460 
#>  noncentral_t_parm            2.853
#>  actual_power                 0.805

# Realized power with 25 clusters per arm
ss_power_mixed_effects(true_smd = 0.30, cluster_size = 30, true_icc = 0.05,
                       specified_n_clusters_per_arm = 25)
#>  term                         value
#>  specified_n_clusters_per_arm 25   
#>  total_N                      1500 
#>  noncentral_t_parm            3.712
#>  actual_power                 0.953

# directional test
ss_power_mixed_effects(true_smd = 0.30, cluster_size = 30, true_icc = 0.05,
                       desired_power = 0.80, directional = TRUE)
#>  term                         value
#>  necessary_n_clusters_per_arm 12   
#>  total_N                      720  
#>  noncentral_t_parm            2.571
#>  actual_power                 0.801
